questions.solution:
Option (c) is the correct choice.

RULE - If the given sentence in Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense, the same sentence in Direct Speech would be in either Present Perfect Continuous Tense or Past Continuous Tense or the same tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had + been + V1-ing + Object) would be converted into Present Perfect Continuous (Subject + has/have + been + V1-ing + Object) or Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object).

Here is the case of Past Perfect Continuous Tense to Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

For example:

He said that they had been waiting for hours. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "We have been waiting for hours". (Direct Speech)

Also, when changing the sentence from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech, usually used conjunction 'that', between the reporting verb and the speech, is removed.

The following changes will be made in the sentence when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
ToldSaid to
SheI
Hadhave
The previouslast

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'She was' becomes 'I am', 'her' becomes 'my' and 'that' is removed.

Accordingly, the option that has the correct Direct speech sentence is (b), Ruchi said, "I am going to cast my vote".

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb [been] and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Perfect tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Perfect tense.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

For example:

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Let I join all your other friends in wishing you a happy birthday.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Let I join all your other friends in wishing you a happy birthday.
questions.solution:
We can only use objective pronouns after the verb 'let'. According to this, the use of the subjective pronoun 'I' is grammatically incorrect. Therefore, the objective pronoun 'me' should replace 'I' to rectify the given sentence. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Let me join all your other friends in wishing you a happy birthday.

Note:

Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party.

Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

'Can' is a modal verb and modal verbs are followed by a base form of the verb, so the use of 'have' is correct here. All the other options are incorrect here [a) is the -ing verb and d) is the past form of the verb].

Note/-

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as a possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. questions.solution:
Rule: The determiners (a word that introduces a noun) "much" and "many" have different usage with respect to countable and uncountable nouns. "Much" is used to introduce uncountable nouns, while "many" introduces countable nouns.

Option b) is correct because "friends" is countable, and "many" is used for countable nouns.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Option a) is incorrect because "much" is used for uncountable nouns, not countable ones like "friends."

Option c) is incorrect because "a lot of" should be followed by plural noun "friends", and not singular "friend".

Option d) is incorrect because the infinitive marker "to" is to be followed by base verb, and not the -ing form of verb.

Note: Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

Immunity is of two types: (i) Innate immunity and (ii) Acquired immunity.

Innate immunity is non-specific type of defence that is present at the time of birth. This is accomplished by providing different types of barriers to the entry of the foreign agents into our body. Innate immunity consists of four types of barriers. These are -

Physical barriers: Skin on our body is the main barrier which prevents entry of the microorganisms. Mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts also help in trapping microbes entering our body.

Physiological barriers: Acid in the stomach, saliva in the mouth, tears from eyes - all prevent microbial growth.

Cellular barriers: Certain types of leukocytes (WBC) of our body like polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils) and monocytes and natural killer (type of lymphocytes) in the blood as well as macrophages in tissues can phagocytose and destroy microbes.

Cytokine barriers: Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection. Hence, all statements are correct.

The combination of the three features listed in the question is unique to and characteristic of the Phylum Echinodermata.

Spiny Endoskeleton: Echinoderms (which means "spiny skin" in Greek) possess an internal skeleton, or endoskeleton, made of calcareous plates or ossicles, located just beneath the skin. In many species, such as sea urchins and starfish, this gives rise to the characteristic spines or bumps on their surface.

Radial Symmetry in Adults: A hallmark of this phylum is the presence of radial symmetry in the adult form, typically pentaradial symmetry (five-part arrangement). This is a secondary adaptation, as their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

Water Vascular System: This is the most distinctive feature of echinoderms. It is a unique hydraulic system of fluid-filled canals that branch into numerous tube feet. The system is used for locomotion, feeding, gas exchange, and sensory reception.

Let's analyze why the other options are incorrect:

(a) Porifera (Sponges): They are asymmetrical, have a simple cellular level of organization, and possess a system of pores and canals for filter-feeding, but they lack a true endoskeleton and a water vascular system.

(b) Cnidaria (Jellyfish, corals): They have radial symmetry but lack an endoskeleton and a water vascular system.

(d) Chordata (Vertebrates and others): They are characterized by a notochord and are bilaterally symmetrical. They do not have a water vascular system.

Further Insights:

Examples of animals in the Phylum Echinodermata include starfish (sea stars), sea urchins, sand dollars, sea cucumbers, and brittle stars.

Echinoderms are exclusively marine animals.

They possess a remarkable power of regeneration, with some starfish able to regrow an entire body from a single arm.

Statement 1 is correct

· GDP per capita is a statistical average obtained by dividing total GDP by total population.

· It is widely used as a proxy indicator of standard of living, especially in cross-country comparisons.

Statement 2 is incorrect

· GDP per capita does NOT capture income distribution.

· It can rise even when income gains are concentrated among a small elite, masking inequality.

· Measures like Gini Coefficient or Lorenz Curve are required to assess income disparities.

Further insights

· GDP per capita is an average measure, not a measure of individual income.

· A high GDP per capita can coexist with high poverty and inequality.

· It is more useful for international comparison than domestic welfare assessment.

· GDP per capita ignores non-monetary aspects like health, education, and well-being.

· Human Development Index (HDI) improves upon GDP per capita by including social indicators.
